No — if I have to answer yes or no, I would say it was not fair to young people.

The 13th AHV/IV pension is a permanent transfer to current pensioners. Your grandson does not pay it directly through his AHV deduction; the legal payer is an employer surcharge. But employer payroll costs are not socially free: they can show up as slower wage growth, lower investment, weaker competitiveness, or pressure on employment. A 22-year-old apprentice is exactly the kind of worker with less power to absorb that.

I would not call it illegitimate: it was approved by voters, and older people are also part of the political community. But “democratically legitimate” and “fair to young people” are not the same thing. On substance, I understand your grandson’s discomfort: it gives a visible benefit to an older group while imposing a hidden cost on a younger, lower-paid group.
